To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electron spin phase-memory relaxation time in the crystalline and glass states of a nitroxyl radical in ethanol is dominated by the coupling with the boson-peak modes of the lattice at low temperatures.
the electron spin relaxation in the molecular glass of ethanol is dominated by the coupling of the spin to boson peak excitators of the lattice.
the electron phase-memory time in a nitroxyl radical is strongly influenced by low-frequency lattice excitations in molecular solids at temperatures below ∼20K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the dynamics of a molecular system at very low temperatures.

the investigation of the electron spin dynamics of a nitroxyl radical in molecular solids at cryogenic temperatures, with particular emphasis on the role of the coupling between the spin degrees of freedom of the paramagnetic probe and the boson peak of the lattice.
the study of the electron spin relaxation in a molecular solid at low temperatures, which is relevant to a wide range of applications, such as spintronics and quantum computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electron spin phase memory time is not only sensitive to the presence of the boson peak but also it can be a probe for the transition between the slow to fast regimes of molecular motion in the glassy and crystalline states.
the fast motion of the nitroxide in the molecular solid at low temperature is a manifestation of the coupling of its electron spin with boson peak excitational modes of the lattice.

the transition from slow to fast motional regime of the nitroxide spin probe in the glassy state of ethanol at temperatures below 20 K is not due to hyperfine coupling with methyl protons, but rather to the coupling of the electronic spin with the bosonic excitations in the lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron phase-memory time of a nitroxyl radical in a molecular glass is a sensitive tool to detect the presence of boson peak excitational states of the lattice.
the electron phase memory relaxation time of the spin probe is a good indicator of the onset of fast motions in molecular solids.
the electron spin relaxation in the system under study is governed by the coupling of the paramagnetic electron with the boson mode excitations of the host matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition from slow to fast motional dynamics of a nitroxyl radical in molecular solids is not necessarily associated with the onset of the glassy state.

the electron spin can be a sensitive probe of fast motion in molecular solids, and that the relaxation dynamics of the electron phase-memory can be a useful probe of the coupling of electrons to boson peak excitons in molecular systems.
, at least for some molecular solids, the slow-to-fast transition of the paramagnetic centers occurs at temperatures below those at which the glass transition occurs.
